messages.subject: blavInspect(object, "lvs") - ERROR non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.subject_clean: blavInspect(object, "lvs") - ERROR non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am trying to get latent variable (factor score) draws using blavInspect(object, "lvs"), but I keep getting an error saying Error in i * rorig : non-numeric argument to binary operator.

I have been able to successfully get  blavInspect(multigroup.invariance.strict,"mcmc") to run, so I'm not sure what the disconnect is. Maybe missing data impacting things? We do have a fair amount of missing data in this data set.

Also, can you clarify whether  blavInspect(object, "lvs") will produce mcmc objects for latent variable means, variances and covariances? Ultimately, this is what I'm after.

Thanks so much!

Best,

DeAnne

messages.subject: Re: blavInspect(object, "lvs") - ERROR non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.subject_clean: blavInspect(object, "lvs") - ERROR non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.body_plain:
DeAnne,

Thanks for the report. I think there is a bug in blavInspect(,"lvs") when you have multiple groups and missing data. That should be fixed soon.

But I am not sure whether you need that command. If you want the overall means/variances/covariances of the latent variables (as opposed to person-specific means and (co-)variances of latent variables), then that should be available from blavInspect(,"mcmc"). The latent variable means would be the alpha parameters, and the (co-)variances would be the psi parameters.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
The posterior samples from blavInspect(, "mcmc") come out in a list object, where there is a separate matrix per chain. To change it to a single matrix (which could be written to csv), you could do

samps <- blavInspect(my_model, "mcmc")

sampmat <- do.call("rbind", samps)

Ed

messages.body_plain:
blavaan 0.4-3 is now on CRAN. You will hopefully notice speed-ups for many models. There are also some new target options: target="vb" for variational Bayes and target="cmdstanr" to use the cmdstanr package instead of rstan. In both cases, the model from target="stan" is used.

Ed

messages.subject: Modeling heterogenous treatment effects in blavaan
messages.subject_clean: Modeling heterogenous treatment effects in blavaan
messages.body_plain:
I'm working with a model in blavaan to estimate the effect of an observed, binary treatment on two (crrelated) latent factor outcomes. I'm particularly interested in modeling the heterogeneity of the treatment effects across pre-treatment variables. The model include strong predictors of the outcomes in the regressions to improve precision.

So far, I have include many-dimensional interactions between exogenous, observed covariates and my treatment indicator in the regression equations to model heterogeneity. However, (a) the selection of variables (and functional forms) is admittedly arbitrary and (b) I'm concerned that I will likely overfit without sufficient regularization. I'm not very familiar with approaches to modeling heterogeneity within the Bayesian SEM framework.

Within the blavaan syntax, do you have any advice for inducing sparsity in the regression equations or reducing parametric assumptions? One idea has been to use Laplace priors on each parameter to induce sparsity. Perhaps there is some way to parameterize this and use a hierarchical prior on the treatment effect coefficients? There are ways apparently to incorporate Gaussian processes into SEM per this article <https://proceedings.mlr.press/v9/titsias10a/titsias10a.pdf>.

Thank you.

messages.subject_clean: Modeling heterogenous treatment effects in blavaan
messages.body_plain:
Hi

My first idea would be to model the SEM as multiple group SEM, this way you can estimate all the parameters being different between treatment groups. Which would save you all the interactions in the regression, and allows you esto estimate measurement model differecnes between groups. What is your total sample size, and for each group? What is you blavaan model syntax so far?

You can regularized the regressions lopes by adding more strict priors of the slopes, with the default stan estimation, you can only use the normal distribution for this. In blavaan you cannot have hierarchical priors. For this you would need to write the model code in stan or jags yourself. This is because blavaan is build to use for general model, with model flexibility, but it is very complicated to add avery possible modification

Not sure what you mean by "inducing sparcity in the regression"? What parametric assumption do you want to relax?

take care
